s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pelvic pain with abdominal mass and recent aggravation
salient_findings: 10 cm mass palpable in pelvic cavity, fixed to anterior rectum
Hard texture and significant tenderness of the mass
Multiple nodules in pelvic area on MRI and CT
key_facts: 40-year-old woman with 8-year history of right lower abdominal pain
Recent aggravation of pain and abdominal expansion sensation
Surgical history includes multiple procedures for fibroids and ovarian cysts
Patient has a 2-year smoking history but quit 5 years ago
Abdomen is soft and tender in lower part without rebound tenderness
Pelvic examination reveals a fixed mass with clear boundary and limited mobility
Rectal examination shows a hard, mobile, non-tender mass 7 cm from anus
CA125 level is 35.08 U/ml
Hormone levels are LH 44.87 IU/L, FSH 108.8 IU/L, Prolactin 6.62 μg/L, Progesterone 0.16 ng/mL, Estradiol <15 pg/ml, Testosterone 12.08 ng/dL
Biopsy results show smooth muscle tumor
Immunohistochemistry is positive for CD34, SMA, desmin, focal CD10, ER, PR, and 2% Ki-67

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth muscle tumor with high Ki-67 index and recent aggravation of symptoms

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with clear boundary and limited mobility, consistent with desmoid tumor characteristics

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large pelvic mass with significant tenderness and fixed to anterior rectum, consistent with aggressive angiomyxoma presentation

shortlist.label: Uterine carcinosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple surgeries for fibroids and ovarian cysts, with recent increase in CA125 level

shortlist.label: Ovarian cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with uneven signals on MRI and inhomogeneous enhancement on CT, raising concern for ovarian cancer

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a fixed mass with clear boundary and limited mobility, along with the biopsy results showing smooth muscle tumor and immunohistochemistry positive for CD34, SMA, desmin, focal CD10, ER, PR, and 2% Ki-67, is consistent with aggressive angiomyxoma. The tumor's location and attachment to the anterior rectum also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The low Ki-67 index (2%) is not typical for leiomyosarcoma, which usually has a higher proliferation rate.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: The presence of a high CA125 level and the tumor's location and attachment to the rectum are not typical for desmoid tumors.

rejected.label: Uterine carcinosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient has undergone total abdominal hysterectomy, making uterine carcinosarcoma unlikely.

rejected.label: Ovarian cancer
rejected.why: The patient has undergone right adnexectomy and the tumor is attached to the rectum, making ovarian cancer less likely.
